speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with a generalized nonpruritic rash, high fever, and a recent seizure. To understand the underlying cause, how long have you had the fever, and did you experience any headache or neck stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The clinical presentation of a high fever lasting 3-4 days followed by the resolution of fever and the onset of a generalized, non-pruritic rash in an infant under 2 years old is classic for this condition, which is caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) or 7 (HHV-7) and can be associated with febrile seizures.
